input.claim_text: On 9 February 2024 I woke up to find someone had spray-painted graffiti all over our front fence and garage door overnight. I haven't had anyone come out to quote on repainting or replacing the panels yet, so I don't have a cost figure at this stage.

input.query: Is malicious damage/vandalism/graffiti to fences or garage doors covered?

output.answer:
Based on the excerpts provided, malicious damage is covered under the NRMA Home policy, but with some limitations noted:

**General coverage:** Malicious Damage is covered "as deliberate or intentional act (including vandalism and a malicious act) but not by You, Your Family or anyone who normally lives in Your Home including a tenant" [NRMA Home KFS, page 1].

**Fences specifically:** The excerpts note that "fences or gates" fall under Building insurance but with the caveat "(limits may apply)" [NRMA Home PDS, page 10], indicating there may be sub-limits on cover for these items, though the specific dollar limits are not shown in the excerpts provided.

**Garage doors:** The excerpts do not specifically mention garage doors in relation to malicious damage cover, so I cannot confirm whether they are treated differently from other building elements.

**Important caveat regarding fences:** Under the "Escape of water or liquid" section, there is a reference to "gates, fences or free-standing walls if the loss or damage was caused because..." [NRMA Home PDS, page 14], but the text is cut off in the excerpt, so I cannot determine what specific condition or exclusion applies here — this appears to relate to escape of water rather than malicious damage, but the excerpts don't provide enough detail to be certain this doesn't also carry over restrictions relevant to other perils.

**Conclusion:** Based on the excerpts, malicious damage/vandalism to fences appears to be covered under Building insurance, subject to unspecified limits [NRMA Home PDS, page 10; NRMA Home KFS, page 1]. However, the excerpts do not contain enough information to confirm the specific limit amounts for fences, nor do they explicitly address garage doors or graffiti as a distinct type of damage. I cannot guess these details — you would need to consult the full PDS for the specific limits table and any additional exclusions that may apply.
